contract.direct_answer:
The evidence bundle only tells us *which niches hold the relevant data*, not a step-by-step Morpheus import recipe, so what follows is a workflow scaffold anchored to the retrieved niches rather than a validated procedure.

The two boundary-condition inputs map to two different niches:

1. Basal-membrane geometry → this is a tissue/boundary specification. The most relevant sources are RN10 (Tejidos chaperones y boundary conditions), which stores Cartesian coordinates of neighboring tissues + timing matrices as .json, and RN6 (Biomecánica pasiva y ECM), which holds basal cortical tension and regional stiffness data. In Morpheus terms, a basal-membrane geometry is expressed inside <Space>/<Lattice> via a domain/membrane image (e.g. a TIFF/image-based domain or a MembraneProperty), or as a fixed CellType/MembraneProperty whose shape comes from the imported coordinates. Concretely: convert the RN10 Cartesian coordinate .json into a raster/label image (or a set of node positions) and load it as the simulation Domain / a boundary CellType, so the membrane contour becomes a no-flux or fixed boundary.

2. AFM stiffness map → this is a passive-mechanics / ECM field. The relevant source is RN6 (Biomecánica pasiva y ECM: affinity matrices, basal cortical tension, cell-friction coefficients as .json; regional stiffness). In Morpheus, a spatially varying stiffness map is represented as a <Field> (a lattice-resolved scalar) or as position-dependent parameters (cortical tension / friction) attached to CellTypes. You would resample the AFM map onto the Morpheus lattice and bind it either as a <Field> initialized from the stiffness raster, or as per-cell/per-segment cortical-tension and friction coefficients drawn from the RN6 .json affinity/tension/friction matrices.

Assembly sketch (not verified against a Morpheus schema in this bundle):
- Import RN10 geometry → Morpheus <Space><Lattice>/<Domain> (image- or coordinate-based boundary) and/or a fixed boundary CellType.
- Import RN6 regional stiffness → a <Field> on the same lattice; import RN6 cortical-tension/friction/affinity matrices → CellType MembraneProperty / interaction (adhesion) and friction parameters.
- Ensure both are resampled onto a common lattice/coordinate frame before binding as boundary conditions.

I cannot give exact Morpheus XML element names, units, or a guaranteed-correct import path from this bundle — those would need the RN13 Morpheus .xml templates (which the retrieval lists as existing but whose contents were not provided).</parameter>
